messages:
maria: Heads-up — I ran a microbench and saw KV-driven OOMs during continuous-batch admit on Llama-2-13B q4. Trying a 'trim-on-admit' heuristic to clip prefix KV entries before batch materializes. Repro steps + profile below.

lee: Can you paste the repro and the top-line numbers? p95 latency / memory?

maria: Repro: ramp up 200 simultaneous short chat streams with long context reuse (avg prefix 12k tokens). Baseline batcher admitted ~1200 tokens/batch then crash. With trim-on-admit (drop old KV pages until token-credit bucket <= target) crashes stop.

maria: Profile snippet (dev profiler):
```
admit_handler: 12.3ms
kv_merge: 48.9ms  mem+30% @ admit
kv_prefetch: 21.0ms
kernel_select: 4.5ms
total_mem_rss: 28GB -> spike 36GB during admit
```

aj: Interesting. So the OOM is squarely at the admit path when we materialize merged KV pages. That aligns with a kernel selection regression where the preferred fast kernel temporarily duplicates buffers.

sam: Do we have a config prototype for trim-on-admit? Something we can A/B roll in canary?

maria: Yep — prototype config I used:
```
{
  "continuous_batcher": {
    "token_budget": 800,
    "admit_trim_target": 600,
    "kv_trim_mode": "age_and_size",
    "kv_trim_fraction": 0.25,
    "eviction_window_ms": 50
  }
}
```

lee: So token_budget 800 -> we admit until aggregated tokens <=800, then trim to 600 if KV over-subscribed? Clarify semantics.

maria: Exactly. On admit we check estimated KV footprint; if estimated footprint > threshold, we run a fast trim pass removing oldest KV pages until est footprint aligns with admit_trim_target. We also fallback to the lower-memory kernel variant if trimming can't make room.

aj: Kernel fallback plan: prefer fast-fp16 kernel for latency; if admit trim fails or KV prediction > X, route to compact-int8 kernel that avoids duplicate buffers. We need an atomic handoff to avoid double allocations.

sam: Queue policy thought: pre-admit trimming vs deferred soft-evict. Pre-admit prevents spikes but may increase per-request miss rate. Deferred soft-evict keeps latency lower for current batch at expense of higher eviction churn. We should test both under mixed workloads.

maria: I ran both: pre-admit trimming increased steady-state cache misses by ~8% and added ~2ms p95, but eliminated OOMs. Deferred soft-evict reduced misses (~2%) but had rare 2-3 OOM events in 1hr run.

lee: Good signal. What about dynamic token-credit bucket? Could throttle admit rate instead of trimming aggressively. Eg: token_credit = max(0, token_credit - requested_tokens); refill rate tuned to avg eviction rate.

maria: I prototyped token-credit bucket too. With bucket size 2000 and refill 500/s we smoothed spikes but saw latency regressions for tail when many short requests queued. Combining bucket + trim-on-admit seems promising.

aj: Another angle: cheap KV footprint estimator. We currently materialize to get exact size. If we can conservatively estimate (pages * avg_page_size * kernel_factor) we can decide kernel routing without the heavy materialize. That saves memory pressure entirely on admit path.

sam: Agree — add a fast estimator using metadata: page_count, quant_level, sparse_flags. Probabilistic upper bound safe for admission decisions.

maria: Patch I tested uses estimator + trim-on-admit + kernel fallback. Results: no OOMs, p95 latency +1.8ms, token throughput -3%. Acceptable for now.

lee: Nice. Any perf regressions tied to kernel selection change? We should run a short perf sweep to ensure we don't degrade common small-convo case.

aj: I'll run kernel A/B in perf lab tomorrow. Will log: p50/p95 latency, token/sec, mem-peak, kernel-switch overhead.

ci-bot: deploy-check: canary job created for branch maria/trim-on-admit-2026-03-18 — tests queued (unit/integration/soak).

sam: Next steps: 1) add estimator to admit path (non-blocking), 2) wire token-credit bucket + admit_trim config, 3) kernel fallback handshake, 4) perf lab sweep, 5) canary.

maria: I'll open the RFC PR with the config knobs and metrics to watch: cache-miss-rate, admit-failed-count, on-admit-allocs, p95 tail. Anyone want to pair on the estimator tomorrow?

aj: I'll pair at 11am. Put notes in PR. :thumbsup:

lee: Great. If canary looks good we can roll to dedicated region with conservative knobs. Thanks team.
